# Intruder Alarms Bolton 2026 Audit

The audit of intruder alarm systems in Bolton for the year 2026 is governed by a comprehensive framework of British Standards and industry best practices.

The primary standard, BS EN 50131, defines the requirements for the design, installation, commissioning, and maintenance of intruder alarm systems.

This standard mandates a risk-based approach, requiring detailed site assessments and system design documentation.

Additionally, BS EN 50174 addresses the acoustic requirements for alarm sound levels, ensuring that alerts are audible without causing unnecessary disturbance.

The cable infrastructure was designed in accordance with TIA/EIA-568-D standards to ensure structured cabling performance.

Wireless access points were evaluated using Ekahau Wi‑Fi heatmapping tools to verify coverage and signal strength throughout the facility.

All cabling was subjected to Fluke DSX testing to confirm compliance with performance specifications.

The installation adheres to SSAIB and NSI compliance requirements for security system installations.

Testing procedures included both manual verification and automated diagnostics to ensure robust operation.

Results were compiled into a detailed report outlining recommendations and remediation pathways.
